title: Resumable Prefetch + Slim SDK for Tool Routing and Structured Exit (PRD Sketch)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working sketch for a compact, resumable streaming surface and a slim SDK layer that prioritizes: (1) anticipatory prefetch/pipeline for tool calls; (2) structured exit frames for reliable downstream parsing; and (3) ergonomic surfaces for mobile/embedded clients with tight bandwidth/latency budgets.

Context / Problem we see in the field:
- Many teams building on top of Hosted API want low-latency incremental responses but end up with brittle client logic when partial tool outputs arrive mid-stream or when network drops.
- Heavy SDKs that expect full-session state are too large for some customers (mobile, edge).
- Tool-calling flows (external lookups, DB ops, execs) introduce non-deterministic pauses; naive streaming either blocks the entire stream or emits ambiguous partials that break structured parsers.
- Current streaming frames are expressive but clients struggle to resume sessions and reconcile partially-applied tool results.

Goals (measurable):
1) Reduce developer pain integrating tool-calls in streaming by delivering a clear resumable protocol and a slim SDK "call adaptor" with 90% of common patterns covered.
2) Keep incremental median end-to-end latency for short responses (<100 tokens) within current SLO (+/-5%).
3) Support session resume semantics that avoid duplicate tool executions in >=95% of resume cases (heuristic-based dedupe).
4) Limit mobile SDK binary impact: <150KB added when including resumability + framing helpers.

Non-goals:
- This sketch does not attempt to replace full-featured session replication or heavy client-side state stores.
- Not addressing enterprise private-deployment bespoke network topologies here (separate PRD later).

High-level approach:
- Define a small set of incremental frame types (prefix/slate/tool-await/tool-result/commit/exit) with compact wire shapes. Prefer tight enums over free-form tags to reduce client heuristics.
- Introduce a resumable session token (RSS token) and short-lived operation ids for tool invocations; server tracks minimal id -> outcome mapping for resumability window (configurable TTL).
- Prefetch hints: allow clients to attach lightweight prefetch intents for up to N external tools (e.g., "lookup:product:sku:1234") — server will opportunistically schedule prefetch and surface best-effort cached results as "fast-path" tool-result frames.
- SDK: expose a minimalist API: StreamClient.open(...).on('frame', cb).resume(rssToken) plus helpers for tool call reconciliation. Keep public surface intentionally small.

Wire protocol sketch (informal):
- FRAME types (compact):
  - PFX (prefix): early context tokens / partial reasoning
  - SLT (slate): continual text chunk updates (may be coarse-grained)
  - TA (tool-await): indicates model is invoking a tool; includes tool-id, op-id, optional dedupe-hash
  - TR (tool-result): tool-return payload (structured JSON) + op-id + status 
  - CM (commit): model indicates this result applied, can garbage-collect op id
  - EXIT: final structured exit object (versioned schema reference)
- Resume flow: client reconnects with rssToken + last-seen-op-id; server replays frames from last checkpoint and will (a) if an op-id is incomplete, either replay TR if result cached, or re-emit TA to indicate re-invocation pending. Server dedupe uses dedupe-hash when provided.

SDK ergonomics (edge cases we must handle):
- Minimal API surface for constrained environments (browser, mobile):
  - openStream(params) -> returns stream handle
  - onFrame(type, handler) and onError
  - requestToolExecution(toolSpec, opts) -> returns Promise that resolves when TR+CM seen; SDK attaches dedupe-hash automatically (derived from normalized toolSpec)
  - resumeStream(rssToken, lastSeenFrameId) -> replayed frames delivered via onFrame
- Offline-friendly pattern: SDK should expose a "compact snapshot" (small JSON) clients can persist to resume without re-downloading entire message history. Snapshot includes last commit frame id, outstanding ops, and last-seen slate hash. Target snapshot size <2KB for short sessions.
- Backpressure and network adaptivity: SDK exposes simple heuristics for mobile: adaptive-window (n frames buffered) + exponential reconnect backoff with jitter, and transparent auto-prefetch disable on metered connections.

Structured output and schema evolution:
- Exit frame is authoritative final: it contains a small schema id and a JSON-LD-like compact result. We provide a version table and a fallback tolerant-parse recipe for SDKs.
- Compatibility rules: older clients must accept additional unknown fields (forward compatible). Server must include minimal type tags when required.
- Tool-result frames contain small typed-headers (type, version) and a base64-encoded compressed payload to keep streaming boundaries neat.

Operational and safety considerations:
- Prefetch/anticipation must be rate-limited per-session and per-customer to avoid runaway upstream calls. Default: 3 prefetch intents per session, adjustable by plan.
- Deduplication window: server keeps op-id -> result for 60s by default; TTL configurable per-customer. We need to profile memory cost.
- Security: tool op payloads might include customer-sensitive query strings; ensure KMS-encrypted logs and strict redaction in telemetry.

Developer UX + Observability:
- Console: new per-session timeline view that shows frames, tool op ids, and resume events. Also surface prefetch hits/misses.
- Telemetry events: stream.open, tool.await, tool.result, resume.attempt, resume.success, resume-dup-suppressed, prefetch.hit/miss. Include counts + p50/p95 latency of tool ops.

Compatibility and migration path:
- Phase 0 (experimental): opt-in server flag + SDK beta for Node/browser with verbose logging.
- Phase 1 (beta): enable resumable streaming for new endpoints and provide migration guide for existing SDKs. Offer server-side compatibility mode that emits legacy-style SLT frames.
- Phase 2 (GA): default enable for hosted-api with opt-out for legacy customers; provide CLI tool to analyze sessions and recommend prefetch budgets.

Success metrics (initial):
- Integration time for sample app (developer playbook) from 2hrs -> 45min (qualitative goal).
- Resume duplicate tool invocations <5% in end-to-end system tests.
- Prefetch hit rate >40% for catalog-lookup workloads in our pilot partners.
- Mobile SDK size impact <150KB added; memory usage <10MB for live stream.

Risk and open questions (working list):
- How long should server keep op -> result mappings? Memory tradeoffs vs developer correctness.
- Prefetch may introduce stale results — semantics + TTL per-tool? need product policy.
- How to instrument retry semantics so that we avoid double-billing customers for tool invocations? (billing implications)
- Interop with function/tool calling sandboxing and security review: what are the attack surfaces for prefetch?

Next steps (short):
- Run a short spike: implement minimal wire frames on staging and a Node SDK shim to validate resume semantics (2 engineer-weeks). Jira spike: API-RESUME-201 (linked above).
- Write a developer playbook + example app (tiny e-commerce lookup + tool call) and test mobile binary size (1 engineer + DX writer).
- Meet with SRE to cost out op-id caching (SLA / memory tradeoffs) and produce rough cost estimates for 10k sessions / minute.

Notes-to-self / TODOs:
- Add concrete frame wire examples (compact protobuf sketch) — TBD after spike.
- Add recommended default prefetch tool types (search, product-lookup, user-profile) and per-tool TTL suggestions.
- Reach out to Solutions Eng (Tomás) for two pilot customers who have mobile constraints.

References / links:
- Confluence: PRD-STREAM-124 (design notes)
- Jira: API-6789 (server resume backlog), API-6790 (sdk resume support)
- GitHub branch: repo/stream-sdk:feature/resume-prefetch

Appendix: Example event timeline (compressed):
- client: openStream -> receives PFX, SLT chunks
- model: emits TA(op-37) with dedupe-hash h1
- server: prefetch hint resolved quickly -> TR(op-37) arrives mid-stream (prefetch:hit)
- model: CM(op-37) and then EXIT final
- client disconnects after PFX seen but before CM: on resume with rssToken + lastSeenOpId=op-37 server replays TR+CM (no re-exec)

End of sketch — this is intentionally rough. Looking for feedback on: frame set minimalism, dedupe-hash derivation heuristics, and snapshot design for tiny clients.
